event: Mthatha / OR Tambo severe thunderstorms (heavy rain, hail, strong winds), spreading to Amathole, Buffalo City, Chris Hani, Alfred Nzo and Joe Gqabi districts
deaths_text: 6 in Mthatha villages (SABC; Daily Dispatch names six victims aged 2 to 73; GLIDE OT-2021-000210-ZAF). The Watchers (15 Dec) also reported 6 deaths from 'the latest storms' in Amathole/Buffalo City after the earlier OR Tambo storm that left 6 dead; unclear whether these are additional deaths or the same count.
displaced_or_affected: 1,762 households (8,810 people) adversely affected (GLIDE/PDMC assessment); 77 families homeless and 15 partially destitute in KSD (Daily Dispatch); 'hundreds' homeless (SABC)
economic_loss: over R80 million estimated household damage (Daily Dispatch)

sources.title: GLIDE OT-2021-000210-ZAF (South Africa: Severe Thunderstorms - Dec 2021)
Death toll now six after Mthatha storm
Death toll rises to six following heavy hailstorm in Mthatha villages
Severe thunderstorms hit Eastern Cape, claiming 6 lives and damaging more than 1 000 homes

notes: Mostly a wind/hail thunderstorm event; deaths and injuries were largely from collapsing houses, not drowning. Daily Dispatch attributes it to 'heavy rains and strong winds' and reports the Gqunu Bridge washed away; 44 admitted to Mthatha General Hospital. GLIDE classifies it as 'OT' (other), not flood. Date: GLIDE/ReliefWeb say early hours of 12 Dec 2021; the Daily Dispatch article refers to the storm on a Thursday (9 Dec), so the start date may be off by up to 3 days. Include in flood analyses only with a flag.

event: OR Tambo severe storms (cut-off low: heavy rain, lightning, gale-force winds)
deaths_text: 5 (TimesLIVE; Xinhua): 3 killed by lightning (a 7-year-old child, a 36-year-old man and an 18-year-old girl), 1 in a structure collapse in KSD, 1 more in Nyandeni (details not given)
displaced_or_affected: more than 160 families homeless; more than 260 households affected
alert_level: Level 6 (reported by Xinhua as a municipal 'level-6 extreme weather warning')

sources.title: Five die, 160 families homeless after severe storms in Eastern Cape district
Weather-related death toll rises to 5 in South Africa's Eastern Cape

notes: This was mainly a thunderstorm and lightning event; no drowning deaths are reported. Flooding is mentioned only in general terms. Mayor Mesuli Ngqondwana: 'We are deeply saddened by the tragic loss of five lives across our district as a result of the recent severe weather conditions.' Start and end dates are approximate: the deaths happened on a Thursday and a Saturday before 10 Feb. It is a separate event from the 13 Feb storm (next record).

event: Mthatha / OR Tambo storm (heavy rain, hail, strong winds) with street flooding
named_places: Nelson Mandela Drive (near Savoy shopping centre)
deaths_text: 3 confirmed in King Sabata Dalindyebo (Inside Metros); Scrolla/allAfrica headline says 7 killed across OR Tambo district
displaced_or_affected: 106 households affected across the district; 45 people homeless in Silverton; over 110 people homeless in the Winnie Madikizela-Mandela area (Scrolla)
alert_level: SAWS Yellow Level 2 to Orange Level 6 (12-13 Feb)
warning_quote: For the past week, our teams have been on standby because these storms have been raging

sources.title: Storms leave three dead, families homeless in OR Tambo
South Africa: Weekend Storm Kills Seven and Destroys 106 Homes in OR Tambo

notes: This was mainly a wind and hail storm; the causes of death were not reported. Scrolla reports flooding on Nelson Mandela Drive, with all lanes under water, which blocked traffic including ambulances from Mthatha General Hospital. The warning quote is from the OR Tambo mayor. The death toll differs by source (3 vs 7). Temperatures had reached 42 C the week before.

event: Ntuzuma (north of Durban) flash flood, about 50 mm in one hour
displaced_or_affected: families displaced; seven houses still submerged three days later

sources.title: IN PICS | Residents blame blocked drains, construction, dumping for flooded homes after heavy rains

notes: The flood happened on the 'Friday night' before the 24 Feb article, so about 20 Feb 2026. This is a small, local event that was kept because families were displaced. Residents blamed blocked drains, construction uphill and dumping. Zanele Shezi: 'Every time it rains, we face the same situation...The drain is blocked, and we suspect the construction work taking place uphill is making it worse.' Nomthando Nyawo: 'We've heard many promises that it will be fixed, but nothing has been done.' This recurrence framing is relevant to the Recurrence-based urgency category. eThekwini Mayor Cyril Xaba cited 113 houses for flood victims and 400 temporary residential units.
